answer: I can't confirm whether an accent mark is printed. Meteg: none seen. Supralinear accent: uncertain. Above the left (sin) side of the שׂ there is one mark. It is larger and more stroke-like than a plain sin dot, so it could be the sin dot printed elongated, or a sin dot merged with an accent. I can't tell which. Under the letters I see only vowels: sheva under ל, hiriq under י, vocal sheva under שׂ, qamats under ר and tsere under א. I see no separate meteg stroke beside any vowel, including the qamats under ר. Nothing else is marked above or below the word.
visible_evidence: The whole word לְיִשְׂרָאֵל is in the image, with all of its lower points. Under the letters, from right to left: ל has two stacked dots (sheva); the first י has one dot (hiriq); שׂ has two stacked dots (sheva); ר has a T-shaped qamats with only its own short stem and no separate vertical stroke to either side; א has two side-by-side dots (tsere); the final ל has nothing under it. No other ink is close to the lower points, so I don't think anything is bleeding in from a neighboring line. Above the word, the only mark is the one over the left of the שׂ. It looks slightly elongated or slanted rather than round. Because of that shape, I can't decide between a plain sin dot and a sin dot plus an accent sign. The meteg-absent reading is fairly clear on its own, at about medium confidence. The question of an accent over שׂ is low confidence.
